vulnerability_mechanism: The SFTP replica client supplied ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey() as ssh.ClientConfig.HostKeyCallback, so ssh.Dial accepted an attacker-controlled server key and exposed SFTP replication credentials and traffic to an active MITM.

protocol.claim_boundary: Stage A establishes causal history without candidate inventory information. A commit is a direct origin only when its own parent lacks the vulnerable SFTP path and its delta creates an independently reachable SSH connection using an unverified host key. Unreviewed or ambiguous candidates remain INCONCLUSIVE.

mechanism_evidence.parent_state: The candidate parent 31da780ed3d372618a6d274c17a41f50f5ada70c has no sftp package or SFTP configuration route.
mechanism_evidence.candidate_delta: The candidate atomically adds the externally configurable SFTP replica route in cmd/litestream/main.go and creates sftp/replica_client.go. ReplicaClient.Init constructs ssh.ClientConfig with HostKeyCallback set to ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey(), then passes that configuration to ssh.Dial.
mechanism_evidence.independent_triggerability: A configured sftp replica reaches ssh.Dial without any server-key comparison; an active network attacker can present an arbitrary host key and terminate the SSH connection.
mechanism_evidence.persistence_to_fix_parent: Blame at fix parent line 84 attributes the surviving InsecureIgnoreHostKey call to this candidate. An ancestry-limited -S/-G search found no later ancestor that removed or reintroduced the callback before the fix.
mechanism_evidence.fix_delta: The fix adds a configurable host-key field, parses it with ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey, and uses ssh.FixedHostKey when supplied. It retains InsecureIgnoreHostKey as an explicit warning-backed fallback when host-key is absent, so the fix enables authenticated SSH but does not make verification mandatory by default.
